title: The Smiling Choir
premise: When her twin brother Milo dies in the village of Hollowmere, Lena Amberdale returns to bury him — only to find the town convinced she is the one who died, and that Milo came home in her place. The sleep recordings she makes to prove her own sanity capture a second voice answering questions in her cadence, a voice that knows things only Milo knew. As frost spreads in patterns across every window and mirror, Lena discovers Hollowmere's choir has sung the same hymn for two hundred years, trading one member each winter for the village's survival. To escape, she must learn the song's forbidden last verse without singing along — because anyone who sings it joins the choir forever. In the end, Lena chooses to sing the verse alone, taking Milo's place in the choir so his ghost can finally leave, and walks out of Hollowmere humming a tune she can no longer remember.
about_author: Vesper Whitlock is the pen name of a former hospice night nurse who spent years listening to what patients said in their sleep. They write horror about grief, small towns, and the terrible arithmetic of belonging.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Lena arrives in Hollowmere for Milo's funeral and finds her own name carved on the headstone. The villagers greet her with pitying warmth, calling her Milo, insisting the dead twin is standing right there. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: disorientation curdling into defiance as she refuses, on principle, to believe any of it.

chapters.title: Household of Echoes
chapters.summary: Lena stays in the twins' childhood house, where Milo's belongings have been arranged around an empty chair set for her. Neighbors bring casseroles and warnings: don't open the windows at night, don't hum. She begins recording herself sleeping to document her own sanity. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by the house's uncanny hospitality.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Reviewing the first night's recording, Lena hears herself answer questions she never asked — in Milo's intonation, with Milo's memories. The voice grows more fluent each night while her own sleep-talk fades. POV: Lena, interleaved with transcribed recordings. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a horrible tenderness toward the thing wearing her brother's cadence.

chapters.title: The Choir Practice
chapters.summary: Lena attends Sunday service to confront the reverend and witnesses the choir: forty voices singing a hymn whose melody seems to rearrange itself for each listener. One soprano's mouth doesn't move. Afterwards, an old woman tells her the frost 'writes its pattern' before the choosing. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: dread replacing skepticism; her unbelief develops cracks.

chapters.title: Frostwork
chapters.summary: Hard frost covers Hollowmere overnight, ferning across glass in shapes that match the hymn's notation. Lena finds the same pattern scarred into Milo's arm and, worse, beginning on her own wrist. The second voice begs her, through the recorder, not to learn the last verse. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the price of survival becomes literal, written on skin.

chapters.title: What Milo Knew
chapters.summary: Lena interrogates the sleep-voice and pieces together the truth: twenty years ago, the twins witnessed a choosing, and Milo bargained to defer it — deferring it onto Lena, then onto himself, until the debt came due. The voice admits it is what remains of Milo, trapped mid-hymn. POV: Lena with extended dialogue. Emotional beat: grief and rage braided together; forgiveness she isn't ready to give.

chapters.title: The Choosing
chapters.summary: The village gathers in the frozen churchyard as the choir names this winter's tithe: the Amberdale twin, whichever one remains. Lena realizes the townsfolk's confusion was never confusion — they were deciding which sibling to feed to the song. She flees, but the frost follows her, writing verses on every surface she passes. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: betrayal; belonging revealed as predation.

chapters.title: Last Verse
chapters.summary: Holed up in the house with mirrors covered and fires burning, Lena forces the sleep-voice to teach her the final verse — the one that ends the hymn instead of continuing it. Learning it means hearing it endlessly; hearing it means fighting the urge to sing along. Her wrist-pattern completes itself. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: grim focus; survival reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Winter Service
chapters.summary: Climax. On the solstice, the choir comes for her, filling the house with harmony that seeps through walls like cold. Lena walks to the churchyard and sings the last verse alone, voice cracking, refusing the melody's pull to harmonize. The choir falters; the frost stops mid-pattern; Milo's voice rises out of her mouth one final time and goes quiet. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: Humming
chapters.summary: Resolution. The thaw comes early. Hollowmere forgets the Amberdales entirely, doors closing like water over a stone. Lena drives away carrying one inexplicable residue: a tune she sometimes hums without knowing it, and a silence in her chest where the second voice used to be. POV: Lena, final pages drifting toward second person. Emotional beat: survivor's peace laced with permanent loss — the price paid, the memory already fading.
